final_codebook.domain: Subtracting fractions, mixed numbers, and whole numbers with simplification to lowest terms

skills.name: Normalize operands
skills.definition: Rewrite a whole number or mixed number into an equivalent subtraction-ready form before the main subtraction begins.
inclusion_criteria: Tag when a whole number is rewritten as a whole plus 0/d to align with a fractional or mixed-number operand.
Tag when a mixed number with an improper fractional part is converted to an equivalent standard mixed number.
Tag when a solution explicitly separates a mixed number into whole and fractional parts as a preparatory rewrite before subtraction.
exclusion_criteria: Do not tag when the step only finds or applies a common denominator.
Do not tag when the step performs subtraction on already usable forms.
Do not tag final simplification or recombination unless the rewrite is clearly preparing an operand before subtraction.

skills.name: Common denominator conversion
skills.definition: Convert fractional parts to equivalent fractions with a common denominator so subtraction can be carried out.
inclusion_criteria: Tag when a solution finds an LCD or other common denominator for unlike denominators.
Tag when one or both fractions are rewritten as equivalent fractions with that denominator.
Tag in mixed-number problems when only the fractional parts are converted to a common denominator.
exclusion_criteria: Do not tag when denominators are already the same and no explicit conversion step is performed.
Do not tag when a whole number is rewritten as n + 0/d; that is operand normalization.
Do not tag when the step only subtracts, borrows, simplifies, or combines results.

skills.name: Subtract aligned parts
skills.definition: Subtract fractions with like denominators and/or subtract the whole-number and fractional parts once the operands are aligned.
inclusion_criteria: Tag when a solution subtracts numerators of fractions that already share a denominator.
Tag when a solution subtracts whole parts and fractional parts separately in a mixed-number or whole-number context.
Tag when the step computes the initial difference, including an intermediate negative fractional part before any regrouping.
exclusion_criteria: Do not tag when the main action is rewriting operands into a new form.
Do not tag when the main action is finding a common denominator or converting equivalent fractions.
Do not tag when the step only borrows/regroups, simplifies, or recombines the final answer.

skills.name: Regroup and simplify
skills.definition: Borrow from the whole part when needed and express the result in lowest terms or appropriate mixed-number or integer form.
inclusion_criteria: Tag when a solution borrows 1 from the whole part and converts it into denominator-sized fractional units to continue subtraction.
Tag when a solution simplifies a resulting fraction or zero fraction to lowest terms.
Tag when a solution combines whole and fractional parts into the final mixed number or integer after subtraction.
exclusion_criteria: Do not tag straightforward subtraction steps that do not involve regrouping, simplification, or final recombination.
Do not tag initial operand rewriting before subtraction.
Do not tag common-denominator work before subtraction.

decisions.reasoning: This skill had 3/3 consensus and is independently testable in items that require rewriting a whole or mixed number before subtraction (e.g., FS04, FS07, FS19) without necessarily requiring common-denominator conversion.

decisions.details: Renamed C02 from 'Common denominator conversion' to S02 'Common denominator conversion' with harmonized wording
decisions.reasoning: The concept was already stable across experts; only minor wording was standardized for clarity. It remains distinct from subtraction itself under the non-redundancy principle.

decisions.details: Refined C03 into S03 'Subtract aligned parts' to explicitly include initial negative fractional differences before regrouping
decisions.reasoning: All experts agreed on the core subtraction skill, but dossier evidence shows some steps produce an intermediate negative fractional part before borrowing (e.g., FS10 Step2, FS13 Step3). Clarifying this boundary improves annotation consistency.

decisions.details: Refined C04 into S04 'Regroup and simplify' while retaining both borrowing and final simplification/combination in one skill
decisions.reasoning: Borrowing/regrouping and final simplification/combination frequently co-occur and are not independently well-separated in this item set. Merging them preserves minimality and identifiability while matching the unanimous expert structure.

summary: The three expert codebooks were already in near-perfect agreement, so the final consolidation preserves the same four-skill structure. Minor refinements were made to sharpen boundaries: S03 covers the actual subtraction step, including intermediate negative fractional results, while S04 covers regrouping plus final simplification/recombination. This yields a complete, minimal, and diagnostically useful 4-skill codebook for fraction and mixed-number subtraction.
